I've saved the results to `answer.json`. I ran the analysis script once and checked one thing in the data: every paid order has at least one line item, so the per-order average in g isn't skewed by empty orders.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment in Q3 (net sales) | consumer, 308,902,384 |
| b. Customers with a paid order in Q3 | 247 |
| c. Top category in Q3 (net sales) | acc, 403,639,439 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the most refunds in Q3 | u64@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders in Q3 | 239 |
| g. Average net sales per order in Q3 | 723,134 |
| h. Net sales growth, August → September 2025 | -3.5% |

- **Segment (a):** consumer finished just ahead of smb, which had 307,396,999.
- **Customer counts (b, e, f):** I counted customers by email. The 300 accounts have 250 distinct emails, so accounts sharing an email were treated as one person. Email case and spacing were already consistent.
- **Segment per order:** each order is grouped under the segment of the account that placed it, after trimming spaces and lowercasing.
